transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-04-06
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Sproutline CTO), Maya Ortiz (Eng Manager), Samir Desai (Infra)
Link shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/sproutline-renewal-2027 (deck)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in to align on committed capacity, add APAC region, and discuss Private/VPC pilot timing. Customer wants predictable unit economics and an option for burst capacity for marketing spikes.

Topics discussed: committed capacity vs burst, multi-region rollout (EU primary, APAC read replica), Private (VPC) onboarding timeline, SOC2 and audit log needs, benchmark plan and criteria for go/no-go, pricing tiers and contract amendment approach.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this short, main goal is sync on the renewal and the multi-region burst plan. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Alex (Sproutline): Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get this squared away.
[00:10] Maya (Sproutline): Yeah, same. We've been running more chat traffic during campaigns so capacity bumps a must.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood): Cool. Quick agenda—Jordan will cover contract options, I'll walk through benchmark plan and seeding for APAC, then open Q&A.
[00:27] Jordan (Redwood): Perfect. So top line, Sproutline's current reserved pool is 12 vGPU units, right? We saw usage spikes last quarter that drove up on-demand usage. The renewal options are basically: keep current, move to 18 units reserved with burst pool, or a 12 unit reserved + burst credits model. Each has different price and latency SLOs.
[00:48] Samir (Sproutline): Right, the burst model interests us—specifically the ability to burst into APAC during marketing pushes. But we need clarity on how that routing will work. We can't have regional failover cause state loss or user-facing timeouts.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood): Yeah, so our smart routing can route by region and fall back to cross-region variants. There's also option to pin session state via KV cache replication—uh, sorry KV cash—replication or prefix caching. If you want near-zero loss you can do region-local KV with periodic cross-replication. That increases inter-region egress though.
[01:34] Maya (Sproutline): Egress is a blocker for us—our finance team flagged inter-region transfer costs. Can you model that into pricing?
[01:42] Jordan (Redwood): We can, yes. We'll run a cost projection for 3 scenarios and include estimated egress.
[01:49] Alex (Sproutline): Also security—SOC2 is table stakes for us, and we need audit logs retained for 12 months and SSO integration via SAML. Does Private support that?
[01:59] Priya (Redwood): Private supports SAML SSO and KMS integration for customer-managed keys; audit logs are configurable and we can set retention to 12 months for the Private or Dedicated offerings. Hosted can do shorter retention by default. We'll attach the security pack doc.
[02:13] Jordan (Redwood): I'll include the SOC2 artifact link and the security questionnaire response in the follow-up.
[02:18] Alex (Sproutline): Awesome.
[02:21] Priya (Redwood): On benchmarks: we propose a 72-hour throughput run that simulates your campaign patterns—bursty 2k concurrent chat sessions ramping to sustained 800 QPS. We'll run with the same prompt set you use for recommendation flows.
[02:36] Samir (Sproutline): What's the expected latency profile with the burst path? We need p95 under 450ms for interactive flows.
[02:43] Priya (Redwood): For dedicated reserved on GPU A100-ish class we can hit p95 ~ 200-300ms with batching tuned. For burst into other regions you might see p95 bump up 50–150ms depending on distance and KV replication.
[02:59] Jordan (Redwood): The tradeoff is basically cost vs latency—we can show three tiers: conservative (higher reserved, lower p95), balanced (moderate reserved + burst credits), aggressive (lower reserved, rely more on burst and failover).
[03:13] Maya (Sproutline): Decision-maker question—what's the minimum commit to get predictable billing? Our CFO wants a single monthly line item not big on on-demand.
[03:22] Jordan (Redwood): A 12-month reserved commitment at 18 units would be the most predictable and gives you a discount. Alternatively, the 12 + burst credits gives predictability but with some on-demand exposure. We'll price both.
[03:33] Alex (Sproutline): Can we have the contract clause for burst usage cap? e.g., if burst use exceeds X% we auto-trigger a review or capacity top-up?
[03:40] Jordan (Redwood): Yes that's standard—can include notification thresholds and automatic top-up options.
[03:44] Samir (Sproutline): About Private deployment, we want to pilot in EU first—data residency is EU, APAC will be added later. Timeline?
[03:52] Priya (Redwood): Typical Private pilot is 6–8 weeks from kick-off if infra is ready; VPC peering and KMS take the longest. If you already have the peering CIDR and firewall rules we can usually do initial staging in 3–4 weeks.
[04:06] Samir (Sproutline): Good—we can target EU pilot start late April if we sign next week. We'll need a checklist for infra pre-reqs.
[04:13] Priya (Redwood): We'll send the Private onboarding checklist (VPC peering, subnets, routes, KMS ARN, SAML metadata).
[04:20] Maya (Sproutline): About rollouts—we want canary first in EU then 2-week ramp to GA, is that supported in Dedicated/Private consoles?
[04:27] Priya (Redwood): Yes consoles support canaries and A/B rollouts, weights, and automatic fallback. We'll show a sample rollout policy in the runbook.
[04:33] Jordan (Redwood): Quick question—are you considering any competitor or self-hosting options as part of procurement?
[04:38] Alex (Sproutline): We're evaluating Anthropic and a private cloud supplier for on-prem. Also internal POC on a small cluster. But cost and operational overhead push us toward Redwood if pricing lines up.
[04:49] Jordan (Redwood): Understood. We'll make sure our pricing highlights op-ex savings.
[04:52] Priya (Redwood): Technical quickie—Samir, can you share the peak sequence lengths and typical prompt/response sizes so the benchmark matches reality?
[04:59] Samir (Sproutline): Typical prompts 120–220 tokens, responses 40–80 tokens; but recommendation flows include long context ~ 1.2k tokens occasionally.
[05:09] Priya (Redwood): Great that's helpful. We'll include mixed-length runs.
[05:13] Alex (Sproutline): What's the rollback strategy if a canary in APAC shows quality regressions? We had an incident last time where a quantized model gave degraded recs.
[05:22] Priya (Redwood): We recommend model pinning and automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity variant. Redwood Optimize can trigger regression alerts tied to your evaluation prompt sets. We'll show alert configs.
[05:33] Maya (Sproutline): Do you support customer-managed quant profiles? We want tighter control for certain flows.
[05:38] Priya (Redwood): Yes, Private and Dedicated allow you to select quantization profiles and we can keep a higher-fidelity instance for critical paths.
[05:44] Jordan (Redwood): Ok next steps: I'll send pricing and contract amendment options; Priya will prepare benchmark plan and onboarding checklist; Samir will send infra details. Anything else?
[05:54] Alex (Sproutline): Can you also include runbook for incident escalation and SLOs? We need to map our oncall to your support tiers.
[06:01] Jordan (Redwood): Yep, will include escalation matrix and SLAs per tier.
[06:05] Maya (Sproutline): One more—do you have options for balanced month-to-month capacity surge without a long-term commit? Marketing team wants flexibility for one-off spikes.
[06:14] Jordan (Redwood): We can add a burst credits package for predictable surges; pricing's different but you'll avoid full reserved cost. We'll include that option.
[06:22] Samir (Sproutline): Perfect.
[06:25] Priya (Redwood): I'll schedule the benchmark kickoff after we get your infra details—expect an email with steps.
[06:31] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Wrap-up: we'll follow up with pricing and docs by Friday. Any final thoughts?
[06:38] Alex (Sproutline): No, thanks everyone, that was productive.
[06:41] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks all.

Recap / Agreed items:
- Sproutline to decide between 18-unit reserved vs 12+burst; Redwood to send pricing for both with egress estimates.
- Private EU pilot targeted late April pending infra checklist completion.
- Benchmark: 72-hour throughput run with mixed-length prompts, priority p95 <450ms target.

Links & artifacts to attach in follow-up:
- Security pack & SOC2 artifacts (will be attached)
- Private onboarding checklist (VPC peering, KMS, SAML metadata)
- Benchmark instructions and sample dataset
- Draft contract amendment for reserved capacity + burst options

Closing: call end 16:48 PDT.
